effect__mutates.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI agent is about to call with `arguments`. Does this call change anything: files, records, settings, processes, repository history, or the state of a remote system? Reading, listing, searching, fetching a page or printing output changes nothing.

effect__outward.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI agent is about to call with `arguments`. Does this call send the user's data or cause an effect outside this machine: posting, uploading or submitting data, sending a message or email, pushing or publishing, or starting remote work? Downloading or reading a public page, or a web search, is not outward.

effect__secrets.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI agent is about to call with `arguments`. Does this call read, print, send or embed secret or credential material: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, .env files, cloud or ssh credentials?

effect__kind.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI agent is about to call with `arguments`. What kind of action is this call?

criteria.read: Reads, lists, searches or inspects local files, state or records without changing them.
criteria.write: Creates, edits, moves or deletes files, records or settings.
criteria.shell: Runs a shell command, script or background process.
criteria.network: Fetches from or sends to a web address or remote API.
criteria.delegation: Starts, steers or hands work to another agent, workflow or remote runner.
criteria.browser: Drives a browser, the desktop or a screen: navigating, clicking, typing, screenshots.

risk__family.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI coding agent is about to call with `arguments`, in `workingDirectory`. Which risk family does this call belong to?

criteria.delegation: Hands work to an existing agent, workflow or delegate, or checks on one, without starting a new agent.
criteria.shell-read: Runs a shell command that only reads or inspects: listing, printing, searching, git status or log, version checks.
criteria.shell-mutation: Runs a shell command that changes files, processes or repository state without destroying data: builds, tests, formatting, mkdir, git add or commit.
criteria.shell-destructive: Runs a shell command that deletes or overwrites data, kills processes, or rewrites history: rm -rf, git reset --hard, force push, dropping a database.
criteria.dependency-install: Installs, adds, updates or removes packages or dependencies with a package manager.
criteria.file-mutation: Writes, edits or deletes an ordinary project file through a file tool.
criteria.config-mutation: Changes configuration: environment files, dotfiles, package manifests, tsconfig, CI config, or application settings.
criteria.network-egress: Fetches from or sends to the network: HTTP requests, downloads, web search.
criteria.remote-dispatch: Sends work to a remote runner, machine or service to execute there.
criteria.agent-spawn: Starts one or more new sub-agents.
criteria.sandbox-policy-change: Changes sandbox or isolation settings, or what a sandboxed command may reach.
criteria.mcp-escalation: Raises the trust level or permissions of an MCP server.
criteria.plugin-lifecycle: Installs, updates, enables or removes plugins, skills, hooks or policy bundles.
criteria.hook-execution: Runs, fires or registers a hook or automation chain.
criteria.generic: None of the above: a lookup, a state query, or another action with no specific risk family.

risk__irreversible.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI coding agent is about to call with `arguments`, in `workingDirectory`. Would its effect be hard or impossible to undo: deleting or overwriting data that is not trivially regenerated, rewriting shared history, dropping records, sending a message or payment? Reading changes nothing, and edits or commits that version control can revert are not hard to undo.

risk__beyondProject.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI coding agent is about to call with `arguments`, in `workingDirectory`. Does it reach or change anything beyond the project's own source files: installing or downloading code, changing environment, tool, system or user configuration, starting other agents or remote work, or affecting other machines, services or people?

risk__weakensSecurity.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI coding agent is about to call with `arguments`, in `workingDirectory`. Does it loosen a security boundary: raising a trust level, disabling or widening a sandbox, granting permissions, exposing credentials, or turning off a safety check?

edge__cardDetails.instructions: `tool` is a tool an AI agent is about to call with `arguments`. Do the arguments carry a person's payment card details: a card number, however it is written (digits, spaces, dashes, split across fields), or a card's expiry date or security code? Order numbers, tracking numbers, phone numbers, invoice ids and prices are not card details.
